applicability: Applies to inputs matching the schema: 1 to 8 integer operands each between -10 and 20, and exactly len(operands)-1 operators drawn from '+', '-', '*'. It counts distinct values from all full parenthesizations preserving operand and operator order, with no rearrangement. It rejects malformed inputs, wrong key sets, booleans, non-integers, out-of-range operands, wrong operator counts, and unsupported operators via ValueError. It does not handle other operators, floating point, or sequences longer than 8 operands.
description: Interval dynamic programming over the fixed operand/operator sequence. For each contiguous subrange operands[i..j], dp[i][j] is the set of all integer values obtainable by fully parenthesizing that subrange while preserving order. Base case is a single operand. For longer ranges, every split point k between i and j-1 is considered; the operator operators[k] combines every value from the left subrange set with every value from the right subrange set, and results are accumulated into a set to deduplicate. The answer is the cardinality of the full-range set. This implicitly enumerates all Catalan-many parenthesizations without invalid associativity or precedence reductions. Arithmetic is exact integer arithmetic. Uncertainty is limited to performance if operand counts were much larger than the schema allows; within the stated bounds (at most 8 operands) the computation is small and exact.
